group.title: Weather and nature
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: With a lot of sun.
examples: It’s a {sunny} day; let’s go to the beach.
wrong: It’s sunny, so the sky is dark and full of rain.

words.meaning: With many clouds in the sky.
wrong: The sky is cloudy, so there isn’t one cloud.

words.meaning: With a lot of rain.
examples: Take an umbrella; it’s a {rainy} day.
wrong: It was a rainy day, so the ground stayed dry.

words.meaning: With a lot of wind.
examples: It’s too {windy} to fly a plane today.
wrong: It’s windy, so the air is completely still.

words.meaning: With thick cloud near the ground, so you can’t see far.
wrong: It’s foggy, so we can see for miles.

words.meaning: Very bad weather with strong wind and rain.
wrong: The storm was calm with no wind at all.

words.meaning: The loud noise in the sky during a storm.
wrong: Thunder is a quiet sound you can hardly hear.

words.meaning: A bright flash of light in the sky in a storm.
wrong: Lightning is a dark shadow in the sky.

words.meaning: A unit for measuring temperature.
wrong: A degree is a unit for measuring time.

words.meaning: One of the four parts of the year, like summer.
wrong: Monday is my favorite season.

words.meaning: The quality of being hot.
wrong: The heat made us put on our coats.

words.meaning: To become hard and cold because of low temperature.
wrong: Water freezes when it boils.

words.meaning: To become liquid because of heat.
examples: The ice cream {melted} in the sun.
wrong: The snow melted in the freezing cold.

words.meaning: To give out bright light.
examples: The sun {shines} all day in summer.
wrong: The sun shines at midnight.

words.meaning: The land next to the sea.
wrong: The coast is in the middle of the desert, far from the sea.

words.meaning: A large dry area with very little rain.
examples: It almost never rains in the {desert}.
wrong: The desert is full of lakes and rain.

words.meaning: Low land between hills or mountains.
wrong: A valley is the top of a mountain.

words.meaning: A line of water that moves across the sea.
wrong: A wave is a small stone on the beach.

words.meaning: Very small pieces of rock, found on beaches.
wrong: Sand is a kind of drink.

words.meaning: A thick forest in a hot, wet country.
wrong: A jungle is a cold place with no trees.

words.meaning: A large round object that moves around a star.
wrong: A planet is a small insect.

words.meaning: Plants, animals and the world not made by people.
wrong: Nature is the inside of a shopping center.

words.meaning: Living or growing without help from people.
wrong: Wild animals live in our kitchen as pets.

words.meaning: One of the very large seas of the world.
wrong: An ocean is a small pond in a garden.

words.meaning: The time when the sun goes down in the evening.
examples: We watched the {sunset} from the beach.
wrong: The sunset happens early in the morning.

words.meaning: The time when the sun comes up in the morning.
examples: We got up early to see the {sunrise}.
wrong: Sunrise is the time when it gets dark.

words.meaning: An area out of the sun, made by a tree or building.
wrong: We sat in the shade to get a suntan.

words.meaning: Wet, soft earth.
wrong: Mud is clean and dry.

words.meaning: A part of a tree that grows out from the trunk.
wrong: A branch is the root of a tree under the ground.

words.meaning: The part of a plant that grows under the ground.
wrong: A root is the flower at the top of a plant.

words.meaning: A small thing that a new plant grows from.
wrong: A seed is a big old tree.

words.meaning: To get bigger, or to make plants get bigger.
wrong: The child grew, so he got smaller.

words.meaning: To take a flower or fruit from a plant.
wrong: I picked a flower by planting a seed.

words.meaning: Very fine dry dirt.
examples: The old books were covered in {dust}.
wrong: Dust is a kind of water.

words.meaning: A large hole in the side of a hill or under the ground.
wrong: A cave is a tall building made of glass.

words.meaning: A place where a river falls over rocks.
wrong: A waterfall is a dry hill.

words.meaning: A small area of still water.
examples: There are fish in the garden {pond}.
wrong: A pond is as big as an ocean.

words.meaning: Changes in the world’s weather, such as rising temperatures.
wrong: Climate change is the weather report for one day.

words.meaning: A light, gentle wind.
examples: A cool {breeze} came from the sea.
wrong: A breeze is a strong storm that breaks trees.

words.meaning: With a lot of snow.
wrong: It was snowy, so the ground was green and dry.
